name: compact-control
title: compactControlClass
description: The geometry of a compact control: a small pill, chip or segment that sits on a line with body text.

files.content:
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'

/**
 * The geometry of a compact control: the size-and-shape half of a small pill,
 * chip or segment that sits on a line with body text.
 *
 * It exists because a settings row does not contain one kind of control. Icon
 * Stack's preview row holds a `SegmentedControl` (pick an appearance), a set of
 * size chips (pick a size) and two on/off pills (watch, monochrome) side by side.
 * Three controls doing the same job at three different heights reads as a
 * rendering fault rather than a design.
 *
 * ## What this owns, and what it does not
 *
 * Geometry only: height, padding, type scale, radius, focus ring, flex. The FILL
 * is the caller's, because the fills genuinely differ and should -- a chosen
 * segment takes the accent, while an active toggle takes a neutral, because "this
 * one of several" and "this is switched on" are different statements.
 *
 * Tailwind's border-box means a caller can add its own `border` without changing
 * the height, so a bordered pill and an unbordered chip still line up.
 *
 * Same reasoning as `optionTileClass` one level down: the shared thing is
 * extracted so the variants cannot drift, and the part that legitimately varies
 * stays with the caller.
 */
export interface CompactControlOptions {
  /**
   * The control sits INSIDE a container that already owns the height -- a
   * `SegmentedControl` segment. It fills that height rather than setting its
   * own, and rounds fully to match the pill riding behind it.
   */
  inset?: boolean
}

/** The height every compact control lands on, container and standalone alike. */
export const COMPACT_CONTROL_HEIGHT = 'h-8'

export function compactControlClass({ inset }: CompactControlOptions = {}): string {
  return cn(
    'wj-focus-ring inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 px-2.5',
    'text-xs font-medium transition-colors',
    inset ? 'h-full rounded-full' : cn(COMPACT_CONTROL_HEIGHT, 'rounded-lg'),
  )
}

docs: Use when a settings row holds more than one kind of small control and they must line up. Icon Stack's preview row has a SegmentedControl, a set of size chips and two on/off pills side by side; each had grown its own padding, and three controls doing the same job at three different heights reads as a rendering fault rather than a design. It owns geometry only -- height, padding, type scale, radius, focus ring, flex -- and leaves the FILL to the caller, because a chosen segment taking the accent and an active toggle taking a neutral are different statements and should look different. Tailwind border-box means a caller can add its own border without changing the height, so a bordered pill and an unbordered chip still align. Pass inset for a control inside an already-bordered container, which fills that height and drops its own radius. Same reasoning as optionTileClass one level down.
